title: Fintrail latency surge — hosted runtime memory fragmentation causing P95/P99 regressions
text:
Fintrail latency surge — hosted runtime memory fragmentation causing P95/P99 regressions

['From: Elena Torres <elena@fintrail.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Fintrail SRE <sre@fintrail.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p99 spike and 502s on /generate - started 08:45 PDT

Priyom —

We started seeing a big latency and error spike this morning around 08:45 PDT for the Fintrail production integration (hosted). P95/P99 for /generate jumped from ~220ms to 2.8s and several requests returned 502. Our SREs pulled traces and saw repeated GPU OOM retries on a small subset of heavy prompts. This is impacting our filings pipeline (batching job).

Can you confirm if there was any change on your side? We’re on model redwood/gpt-large-v1, region: us-west-2. Attached a small trace and a heap indicator from the client side. Let us know urgent next steps — we have a scheduled cut at 11:00 and are taking heat from ops.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Principal SRE, Fintrail

Attachment: trace-logs-20270420.txt (3.2 KB)
', 'From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@fintrail.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spike and 502s on /generate - started 08:45 PDT

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick note and the trace. I’m putting SRE and runtime on this immediately. Initial hypothesis: recent kernel fallback for attention optimization may be increasing fragmentation on longer sequences for that model shape which can surface as transient OOM and retries at the serving layer.

Immediate actions we’ll take:
- Rishi to validate GPU memory fragmentation metrics and force a cache compaction if needed.
- Temporarily route Fintrail traffic to a lower-concurrency pool to reduce KV-cache pressure.
- Collect a server-side heap dump (we’ll request permission before pulling anything sensitive).

I’ll keep you updated within 30 minutes and will add Marissa for exec visibility.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@fintrail.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spike and 502s on /generate - started 08:45 PDT

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 09:35 AM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial hypothesis: recent kernel fallback for attention optimization may be increasing fragmentation on longer sequences for that model shape

Checked the node pool metrics. We see repeated allocation failures and then successful fallbacks that inflate tail latency. Heap histograms show growing free-fragmentation on GPU0/2 across the rack starting at ~08:40. I triggered a live compaction on the affected hosts (INF:trigger/compaction) which dropped the immediate OOM retries.

What we did (10:00):
- Flushed KV cache for Fintrail keys on the impacted pods.
- Forced low-concurrency routing (concurrency cap = 3) for Fintrail tenant for the next 2 hours.
- Captured heap dump and async GPU trace (uploaded to redwood drive link).

Observed result: error rate decreased by ~85% and p99 is down to ~900ms (still above expected). We are continuing to profile kernel selection; a conservative rollback to the prior attention kernel is under evaluation.

Attachment: heap-dump-20270420.bin (1.1 MB, attachment stub)

—Rishi
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fintrail.io>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: sudden p99 spike and 502s on /generate - started 08:45 PDT

Looping in leadership for visibility — Fintrail is a priority account and ops is asking for a formal mitigation plan and ETA.

Key items for exec attention:
- We currently have a temporary throttle in place; need decision on emergency credits and SLA exception for the 11:00 cut.
- Engineering needs permission to revert the attention kernel rollback if profiling shows it reduces fragmentation without regressing accuracy.
- Customer is requesting confirmation of root cause and what we will change to prevent reoccurrence.

Priyom / Rishi: can you prepare a short incident memo and an ETA for a targeted patch? Please include whether a model-variant fallback (quantized variant) would be acceptable for Fintrail given accuracy constraints.

—Marissa
VP, Operations, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@fintrail.io>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spike and 502s on /generate - started 08:45 PDT

Status update (current):

1) Root cause (prelim): high fragmentation on GPU allocator triggered by new attention kernel fallback for medium+long sequences. Fragmentation combined with aggressive pooling caused transient OOM and retry storms on a small subset of heavy prompts.

2) Short-term mitigations applied:
- Low-concurrency routing continues for Fintrail (concurrency cap 3).
- KV-prefix pinning disabled for the largest prompt classes to avoid long-lived cache retention.
- Live GPU compaction performed across affected hosts.

3) Medium-term plan (target timeline):
- Roll back kernel fallback to previous stable attention kernel for the model variant (ETA: 36 hours) — this reduces fragmentation but requires testing for perf/quality.
- Ship a memory-aware allocator patch (INF-1298) that avoids allocation hot-spots (ETA: 2 weeks with staged rollout).
- Offer Fintrail the option to be routed to a quantized model variant with strict accuracy gating during the rollback window (if they accept, we can re-route within 2 hours).

4) Customer ask: Fintrail requested a small credit for the time window and an ops postmortem. I recommend approving a one-time credit and a collaborative postmortem with their SREs.

Elena: if you can confirm whether the quantized variant is acceptable for the batch cut, we can implement the route change ASAP.

—Priyom
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Elena Torres <elena@fintrail.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spike and 502s on /generate - started 08:45 PDT

Thanks for the clear update and for the compaction work. Fintrail accepts routing to the quantized variant for the scheduled batch run this evening — we tested a small sample and saw acceptable token-level accuracy within our gating. Please proceed with the temporary routing and include a list of observable SLOs we can monitor during the window.

We also appreciate the offer of a one-time credit and request the postmortem within five business days. The SRE team will coordinate on reproducing the prompt that surfaced the fragmentation locally (we will share a minimized prompt set).

—Elena
Principal SRE, Fintrail
']
